anf_compare.notes: ANF/NPNF has no text of this letter; translated directly from the PG 77 Greek.

choices.why: πρεσβύτης is 'old man'; the presbyter is πρεσβύτερος. Peter is a bishop, so 'presbyter' would wrongly demote him.

choices.term: τῇ κλήσει τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς / μόνην αὐτῷ τὴν κλῆσιν
choices.english: the very title of bishop / only the title
choices.why: κλῆσις here is the name Peter still bears, as in the previous section ('the name of the priesthood'); 'call' is a calque.

choices.english: For we suppose, perhaps, that we have shown the old man mercy
rejected: for we think to have pity
choices.why: νομίζω with the aorist infinitive: what we suppose we have done; 'think to have pity' is not English.
The word means lacking mutual love; Cyril is speaking to a fellow bishop.
συνίστημι with ὑπόληψις: to vindicate one's repute.

choices.english: the record of the proceedings would itself
choices.why: ὑπομνήματα are the minutes of a hearing; the literal phrase is a calque.

lemmas.gloss: calling; here the title of bishop
old man (here Peter the bishop; not πρεσβύτερος, presbyter)

pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: '…not even by the very] to be honored (τιμάω, pres. pass. inf.) by the calling/title (κλῆσις) of the episcopate (ἐπισκοπή). But perhaps it would seem (δοκέω, aor. opt. + ἄν) to your God-fearingness (θεοσέβεια) that the word from me is somewhat harsh (σκληρός) and without mutual love (ἀφιλάλληλος); but it holds not so according to the truth. For perhaps somehow we think (νομίζω) to have shown mercy (ἐλεέω, aor. inf.) to the old man (πρεσβύτης), having left (ἀφίημι, aor. ptc.) to him the title alone; but by far (μακρῷ) it was better to consider (ἐννοέω) also the other thing. For he asserts (φάσκω) that he is able (δύναμαι) to stand together with / establish (συνίστημι, aor. inf.) his own repute (ὑπόληψις), but did not receive a time/occasion (καιρός) of defense (ἀπολογία), nor indeed (οὔτε μήν) was a canonical (κανονικός) hearing (ἀκρόασις) added (προστίθημι, aor. pass. inf.) for him. And if any such thing had happened, the very composition (σύστασις) of the minutes/records (ὑπόμνημα) would have tested/exposed (διελέγχω, aor. + ἄν) him: either him having been caught (ἁλίσκομαι, aor. ptc.) by the charges (αἰτίαμα), declared (ἀποφαίνω, pf. pass. ptc.) liable (ἔνοχος), and having nothing left to say as one wronged (ἀδικέω, pf. pass. ptc.); or at least, having declared him free (ἐλεύθερος), it was giving (δίδωμι, impf.) again the presiding (προΐστημι, pf. inf.) of the church, which also had come to be under the hand (χείρ) of him. But nothing of such a kind having been done (πράσσω, pf. pass. ptc., gen. abs.), he cries out against (καταβοάω) the affair (πρᾶγμα); he says to have undergone (ὑφίστημι, aor. inf.) unbearable (ἀφόρητος) injustice (ἀδικία), [continues in the next section].
pass_b_english: …to be honored with the very title of bishop. But perhaps what I say may seem to your piety somewhat harsh and unbrotherly; yet in truth it is not so. For we suppose, perhaps, that we have shown the old man mercy by leaving him only the title; but it would have been far better to consider the other side as well. For he says that he could clear his good name, but that he was given no opportunity to defend himself, nor indeed was he granted a canonical hearing. Had anything of the kind taken place, the record of the proceedings would itself have made his case plain: either proving that he had been caught by the charges and declared guilty, with nothing more to say as one who had been wronged, or else declaring him free and giving him back the right to preside over the church that had been placed under his hand. But since nothing of the kind was done, he cries out against what has happened; he says that he has suffered intolerable injustice…
source_text:
τιμᾶσθαι τῇ κλήσει τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς. Ἀλλ' ἴσως δόξειεν ἂν τῇ σῇ θεοσεβείᾳ σκληρὸς
εἶναί τις καὶ ἀφιλάλληλος ὁ παρ' ἐμοῦ λόγος, ἔχει δὲ οὐχ οὕτω κατὰ τὸ ἀληθές·
ἐλεῆσαι γὰρ τάχα που νομίζομεν τὸν πρεσβύτην, μόνην αὐτῷ τὴν κλῆσιν ἀφέντες·
μακρῷ δὲ 278 ἦν ἄμεινον ἐννοῆσαι καὶ τὸ ἕτερον· φάσκει γὰρ δύνασθαι μὲν
συστῆναι τῇ οἰκείᾳ ὑπολήψει, οὐ λαβεῖν δὲ καιρὸν ἀπολογίας, οὔτε μὴν ἀκρόασιν
αὐτῷ προστεθῆναι κανονικήν. Εἰ δ' ἐγεγόνει τι τοιοῦτον, αὐτὴ τῶν ὑπομνημάτων ἡ
σύστασις διήλεγξεν ἂν αὐτόν, ἢ ἁλόντα τοῖς αἰτιάμασιν ἔνοχον ἀποπεφασμένον καὶ
οὐδὲν ἔχοντα λοιπὸν εἰπεῖν ὡς ἠδικημένον, ἢ γοῦν ἐλεύθερον ἀποφήνασα πάλιν
ἐδίδου τὸ προεστάναι τῆς ἐκκλησίας, ἣ καὶ ὑπὸ χεῖρα γέγονε τὴν αὐτοῦ. Οὐδενὸς δὲ
πεπραγμένου τοιούτου, καταβοᾷ τοῦ πράγματος· ἀδικίαν ἀφόρητον ὑποστῆναί φησι,
source_normalizations: 'μακρῷ δὲ 278 ἦν': 278 is the PG column number printed inside the text; it is not translated.
reviewer: claude source review, separate pass (same model family as the drafter)
notes: The section opens mid-sentence: the previous section ends 'not even…' (μηδ' αὐτῇ) and this one supplies τιμᾶσθαι τῇ κλήσει τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς.
The section ends mid-sentence after φησι; the next section continues the reported speech with καὶ ἀθέσμως ἐκβεβλῆσθαι, so the English ends with an ellipsis.
No Scripture quoted or clearly alluded to in this section.

review.coverage: every clause checked against the source
changes: τὸν πρεσβύτην corrected from 'the presbyter' to 'the old man' (Peter the bishop); title changed from 'The Presbyter's Defense' to 'Peter Was Given No Hearing'.
κλῆσις rendered 'title' and αὐτῇ ('the very') restored; συστῆναι τῇ οἰκείᾳ ὑπολήψει corrected to 'clear his good name'.
'the composition of the memoranda' replaced by 'the record of the proceedings'; ἀφιλάλληλος 'unbrotherly'.
Final clause ends with an ellipsis because the sentence continues in the next section.
Justification rebuilt 2026-10-24 to match the corrected English; old machine-draft glosses and choices replaced.
checked: agency: Peter speaks (φάσκει, καταβοᾷ, φησι); Cyril and Domnus are the 'we'
negation: οὐ λαβεῖν … οὔτε μὴν … προστεθῆναι
conditional: εἰ δ' ἐγεγόνει … διήλεγξεν ἄν (contrary to fact)
